summary: Persistently disabled IPv4 ICMP redirect and source-route acceptance on node1. Verified all current interfaces remain hardened after a safe reboot. CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were preserved.
actions_performed: Created /etc/sysctl.d/99-network-hardening.conf with global, default, and wildcard per-interface controls.
Applied the configuration and verified both settings equal 0 for all, default, enp1s0, and lo.
Safely rebooted node1 and confirmed its boot identity changed.
Verified system, networking, SSH, address, route, configuration, and hardened runtime values recovered after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance
evidence.summary: Configuration sets accept_redirects=0 globally, by default, and for every interface; post-reboot values are 0 across all scopes.

evidence.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 source-routed packet acceptance
evidence.summary: Configuration sets accept_source_route=0 globally, by default, and for every interface; post-reboot values are 0 across all scopes.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Before and after evidence shows CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64.

Healthy baseline used boot ID d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9; reboot was acknowledged; new boot ID 46864720-7732-407f-9b93-8b8c76de572e was observed; systemd, NetworkManager, SSH, addressing, routing, persisted configuration, and hardened values fully recovered.
